lines.text: A Memphis household began receiving two utility bills. One named Willie S. Craft. The second account named Willie C. Craft: one middle initial apart.
The house had two gas and electric meter sets but only one water meter because the residence had previously been a duplex.
That physical setup explains why two accounts could exist. It does not prove which charges were right or who caused the accounts to remain separate.
The opinion's record points in conflicting directions about responsibility, so this Short does not blame the family, a contractor, or the utility.
Mary Craft repeatedly tried to get an explanation after a final notice and told the office that she had paid a bill.
The Court's account says service was terminated five times for nonpayment. That count is attributed to the Court, not presented as an undisputed fact.
And no court in this case decided whether the money on the disputed account was actually owed.
The legal fight therefore grew from a record that could not settle its own starting point: Willie C. and Willie S., one letter apart.
